title: Multidisciplinary Software Development (cross-taught with EECS 497: Human-Centered Software Design and Development)
sourceFiles: EECS 497&ENGR455_Human-Centered Software Design and Development & Multidisciplinary Software Development_Winter 2021.pdf
weeklyTopics: Team dynamics, creative problem solving, dealing with failure, leadership, conflict resolution
(second semester continuation topics, for MDP/EECS497 students continuing): security, change management, maintenance, business considerations, case studies, intellectual property, entrepreneurism
workloadNotes: Part of the Multidisciplinary Design Program (MDP): teams pair CS students with non-CS 'domain' students on a real sponsor's project, following the full software design/development cycle from idea to delivery. Fully asynchronous lectures (recorded), with a lecture-summary quiz to verify attendance. EECS 497 grading only (ENGR 455 is graded separately through MDP): Initial Project Concept Doc 2%, Lecture Summaries 5%, Self/Team Evaluations 5%, Project Planning Doc 7%, User Requirements Doc 9%, Lo-Fi Prototype 12%, Testing and Debugging Report 15%, Final Demo 20%, Exam 25%.
textbooks: Holtzblatt, Wendell, and Wood, Rapid Contextual Design, 2008
Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach, 8th ed., McGraw-Hill, 2014
